phase_name: Authority Evaluation Model Core Operational Readiness Assessment
summary: Phase 147I assessed whether the Phase 147H-verified standalone pcae.authority_evaluation implementation is ready to become the subject of a separately governed integration architecture phase, per human authorization following Phase 147H's AUTHORITY EVALUATION MODEL IMPLEMENTATION VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS verdict. Independently re-confirmed the actual public API via read-only research (the 14-symbol __init__.py export surface, the exact seven-parameter evaluate() signature, the single-method AuthorityRegistry ABC with zero concrete implementation, the model/error/serialization shapes) and re-confirmed AuthorityEvaluationRequest and RegistryResolution do not exist anywhere in the package. Reconstructed the surrounding lifecycle (Session, PublicationReadinessPackage, CHGR construction via governance/publication/record.py, the cltr module, and the Decision Template JSON schema) and all nine governing contracts (AEM-001, AEMIC-001 v1.2, IWC-001, IWPC-001, PEC-001, CHGR-001, TAMC-001, TAMPC-001, GAC-001) using three parallel read-only research agents, then synthesized their findings directly. Mapped all seven evaluator inputs: template_ref, template_version, evaluated_at, and evaluator_version already have lawful sources; claimed_identity has no defined source (Session.owner_identity is a distinct, unverified analog); declaration is blocked on a concrete AuthorityRegistry, which AEM-001 itself explicitly deferred building; citation_text is blocked on a Decision Template resolution mechanism that does not exist anywhere in this repository (the schema is descriptive-only, unused by any code). Compared five Registry storage options (favoring a filesystem-backed Registry following the PublicationRecordStore/cltr persistence.py house style), six candidate integration owners (favoring a dedicated application service, explicitly against Publication Coordinator per PEC-REQ-115/116's existing prohibition on the Coordinator performing evaluation), eight evaluation-timing points, and four candidate integration architectures, preferring a two-stage (advisory plus pre-CHGR freshness re-evaluation) model orchestrated by one new, narrowly scoped component that is the sole caller of AuthorityRegistry.resolve(). Confirmed direct gating is forbidden under AEM-REQ-003/037 across all nine contracts, and that CHGR-001's already-reserved authority_basis_claimed field, populated via PEC-REQ-115's existing verbatim-citation mechanism, is the narrowest lawful outcome-consumption path requiring no CHGR-001 schema change. Overall Verdict: CORE OPERATIONALLY READY -- INTEGRATION ARCHITECTURE NOT READY, because claimed_identity sourcing, Decision Template resolution, and the concrete Registry choice remain genuinely undecided, contract-deferred, or entirely unbuilt. Full detail in docs/PHASE_147I_AUTHORITY_EVALUATION_MODEL_CORE_OPERATIONAL_READINESS_ASSESSMENT.md.

validation_results.name: phase_147i_current_state_reconstruction
validation_results.result: Three parallel read-only research agents independently reconstructed (1) the authority_evaluation package's full public API, model fields, exception taxonomy, and serialization entry points; (2) the surrounding lifecycle components (interactive_workflow Session and PublicationReadinessPackage, governance/publication CHGR construction, cltr, and the Decision Template JSON schema), confirming citation_text and claimed_identity have no existing lifecycle source and that authority_basis_claimed is already reserved but disclosed as unpopulated in production code; (3) all nine governing contracts (AEM-001, AEMIC-001 v1.2, IWC-001, IWPC-001, PEC-001, CHGR-001, TAMC-001, TAMPC-001, GAC-001), confirming the exact seven-parameter evaluator-input table, the disclosure-only/non-gating mandate (AEM-REQ-003/037), and PEC-001's existing PEC-REQ-115/116 prohibition on the Publication Coordinator performing evaluation. All three agents' findings, cited with file paths and requirement IDs, were synthesized directly into the report; no finding was delegated to synthesis by an agent.

recommended_next_phase: Recommended next phase: a narrowly scoped prerequisite-decision phase resolving claimed_identity sourcing, a Decision Template resolution design sufficient to unblock citation_text and inform the Registry-option choice, the AEMIC-001 evidence_kind compatibility question, and explicit human sign-off on the two-stage evaluation model -- before any future 147J (Authority Evaluation Model Integration Architecture) phase, which must remain architecture-only throughout.
